a.summary: CONVENTIONS.md claims to be the one place this family of surprises is visible, but has no entry for the createTx caller-array mutation nor for the two earlier declaration-only surprises added in this same review chain.
a.failure_scenario: A contributor follows AGENTS.md:463 ("`CONVENTIONS.md` lists the ones that have already caught people") before writing assertions against `Transaction.createTx`, `Instruction.extraAccounts` or `Instruction.createInstruction`. The file says nothing about any of them, so the contributor writes the reasonable assertion - reusing a sorted array across two createTx calls, or asserting `extraAccounts(List.of((AccountMeta) null))` appends a null - and it fails, which is precisely the failure mode the file's own preamble says it exists to prevent ("several of these were found by writing the *reasonable* assertion and watching it fail").

b.summary: A newly documented caller-visible array-ownership surprise was added at the declaration but not to CONVENTIONS.md, the file whose stated purpose is to make that family visible in one place.
b.failure_scenario: A consumer follows the file's own instruction ("Read this before writing assertions against an API you have not used here") and reads the `## Byte-array ownership` section. It tells them which factories retain an input array and that they can pass `bytes.clone()`. It says nothing about a factory that reorders an input array. They call the four-arg `createTx` with a reused `sortedAccounts`, reuse it afterward, and get the wrong account order — the exact behavior the delta just documented and that uses the same `clone()` remedy the section already teaches.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
